title: Refractive glass text magnifying loupe
blurb: An editable editorial card and textarea drawn on one WebGL 2 canvas with a refractive glass magnifying loupe floating above the caret or pointer. Both the 1:1 page and the zoomed bevelled lens sample the same texElementSubImage2D() texture with no duplicate DOM.
question: Can a spherical refractive glass magnifying loupe sample the exact rendered glyphs, selection highlight, and live caret from a single texElementSubImage2D() upload while dragging or typing inside live HTML text, with no duplicate DOM or selection drift?
result: Measured in headless Chrome Canary 160 (`160.0.8187.0`, 412 px wide at 2.625 DPR, 2026-11-27): all 6 live checks pass on one ElementGL WebGL 2 context (gl.getError() === 0, peak 2 contexts, 1.22 MP canvas), updateElementGeometry() keeps the textarea and swatch buttons clickable across WebGL 2 and the 2D 9-argument clip fallback, and --disable-blink-features=CanvasDrawElement falls back to plain HTML. Android phone touch testing and check:jank are not verified yet.
